result.markdown: --- title: "Session 2 — Adjustment, Bad Controls and Standardisation" subtitle: "Regression adjustment · mediator and collider bias · effect modification · g-computation · ATE and ATT · Lab 2" author: "Community Medicine Workshop" format: revealjs: theme: serif css: [../assets/slide_deck.css, assets/workshop.css, assets/quiz.css] include-after-body: assets/quiz-include.html embed-resources: true slide-number: true navigation-mode: linear code-copy: true center: false transition: fade width: 1280 height: 720 fig-align: center html-math-method: plain execute: echo: true warning: false message: false fig-width: 9 fig-height: 4.6 fig-dpi: 100 --- ## Where we are ::: {.incremental} - Session 1: the DAG says **adjust for** age, sex, education, urban, BMI, diabetes, baseline SBP - Today: **do it with regression**, see what **bad controls** do, and get **ATE and ATT** by **standardisation** ::: # Topic 1 — Regression adjustment {background-color="#2C3E50"} ## Adjusted for the confounders ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} m_adj <- lm(f_out, data = htn) round(c(estimate = coef(m_adj)[["programme"]], confint(m_adj)["programme", ]), 2) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` estimate 2.5 % 97.5 % -6.29 -7.14 -5.43 ``` ::: ::: ::: {.key} **−6.3 mmHg** (95% CI −7.1 to −5.4), against the naive **−1.4**. Confounding **hid** most of the benefit, because the enrolled started with a **higher** SBP. (Because the data are synthetic we know the truth: **−5.8**.) ::: # Topic 2 — Bad controls {background-color="#2C3E50"} ## Adjusting for a mediator or a collider ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} m_med <- update(m_adj, . ~ . + adherent); m_col <- update(m_adj, . ~ . + clinic_visits) round(c(naive = coef(lm(sbp_12m ~ programme, data = htn))[["programme"]], adjusted = coef(m_adj)[["programme"]], plus_mediator = coef(m_med)[["programme"]], plus_collider = coef(m_col)[["programme"]]), 2) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` naive adjusted plus_mediator plus_collider -1.36 -6.29 -2.97 -8.84 ``` ::: ::: ::: {.incremental} - **+ adherence (mediator): −3.0**. Half of the effect has gone: this is only the **direct** effect, **not** what the programme achieves - **+ clinic visits (collider): −8.8**. The effect is **exaggerated** by a non-causal path - Both models have a **higher R²** than the correct one: **fit is not a guide** to causal adjustment - "Adjust for everything available" is **wrong** ::: ## Table 2 fallacy ::: {.warn} In the adjusted model, **only the programme coefficient** has a causal reading. The coefficients of age, diabetes and so on are **not** their total effects (their own confounders and mediators differ). Do not interpret every row of a regression table causally. ::: # Topic 3 — Standardisation {background-color="#2C3E50"} ## The effect may differ between people ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} htn <- htn |> mutate(bsbp_c = baseline_sbp - 150) m_int <- lm(sbp_12m ~ programme * bsbp_c + age + sex + education + urban + bmi + diabetes, data = htn) round(summary(m_int)$coefficients[c("programme", "programme:bsbp_c"), 1:2], 3) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Estimate Std. Error programme -5.888 0.461 programme:bsbp_c -0.092 0.035 ``` ::: ::: The programme lowers SBP by **5.9 mmHg at a baseline of 150**, and by **0.09 mmHg more for each extra mmHg** of baseline SBP. So **which average** do we want? ## g-computation ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} p1 <- predict(m_int, transform(htn, programme = 1)); p0 <- predict(m_int, transform(htn, programme = 0)) round(c(ATE = mean(p1 - p0), ATT = mean((p1 - p0)[htn$programme == 1])), 2) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` ATE ATT -6.17 -6.58 ``` ::: ::: ::: {.incremental} 1. Fit an outcome model (with interactions if needed) 2. **Predict for every adult twice**: as if **enrolled**, as if **not** 3. **Average the difference**: over everybody (**ATE −6.2**) or over the enrolled (**ATT −6.6**) - The ATT is larger: the enrolled have a **higher baseline SBP**, where the programme **works better** - Confidence intervals: **bootstrap** the whole procedure - Works for **any** outcome model (logistic: risk differences and risk ratios) ::: ## Which estimand? | Question | Estimand | |---|---| | Should the programme be offered to **all** hypertensive adults? | **ATE** | | Did it benefit the adults **who enrolled**? | **ATT** | | What happens in adults **like those not yet enrolled**? | ATU (untreated) | ::: {.key} State the **estimand** before choosing the method: regression, matching and weighting can each target **different** populations. ::: ## 🔧 Switch to R — Lab 2 {.lab-slide background-color="#1565c0"} ::: {.lab-box} **File:** `causal-workshop/labs/lab2_adjust.R` - adjusted effect with CI - mediator and collider as bad controls - interaction, standardisation: ATE and ATT ::: **Time:** 35 minutes · answer the Q questions in the comments ## Self-check quiz (1/5) {.smaller} ::: {.quiz-q data-qid="z2q1" data-type="mcq" data-hash="6938fk.y1maku" data-show="VGhlIGVucm9sbGVkIHdlcmUgc2lja2VyIGF0IGJhc2VsaW5lLCB3aGljaCBtYXNrZWQgdGhl IGJlbmVmaXQ=" data-explain="RW5yb2xsZWQgYWR1bHRzIHN0YXJ0ZWQgd2l0aCBhIGhpZ2hlciBTQlAgYW5kIG1vcmUgcmlz ayBmYWN0b3JzLCBzbyB3aXRob3V0IHRoZSBwcm9ncmFtbWUgdGhleSB3b3VsZCBoYXZlIGhh ZCBhIGhpZ2hlciBTQlAuIFRoZSBjb25mb3VuZGluZyB3b3JrZWQgYWdhaW5zdCB0aGUgYmVu ZWZpdC4="} The naive difference is -1.4 mmHg and the confounder-adjusted estimate -6.3 mmHg. Why was the naive estimate so close to zero? - The adjusted model has more parameters, which makes the estimates larger - The naive estimate uses fewer adults than the adjusted estimate does - The enrolled were sicker at baseline, which masked the benefit - The programme has no effect, and the adjustment created one by chance ::: ## Self-check quiz (2/5) {.smaller} ::: {.quiz-q data-qid="z2q2" data-type="mcq" data-hash="693loa.y1mp28" data-show="VGhlIHBhcnQgb2YgdGhlIGVmZmVjdCB0aGF0IGRvZXMgbm90IHBhc3MgdGhyb3VnaCBhZGhl cmVuY2U=" data-explain="QWRoZXJlbmNlIGlzIG9uIHRoZSBjYXVzYWwgcGF0aC4gSG9sZGluZyBpdCBmaXhlZCBsZWF2 ZXMgb25seSB0aGUgZGlyZWN0IGVmZmVjdCwgd2hpY2ggaXMgbm90IHRoZSB0b3RhbCBiZW5l Zml0IG9mIHRoZSBwcm9ncmFtbWUu"} After adding adherence to the model the programme coefficient falls from -6.3 to -3.0. What does -3.0 estimate? - The total effect, now free of the confounding by adherence - The effect of adherence on blood pressure in the enrolled adults - The bias that was present in the confounder-adjusted model before - The part of the effect that does not pass through adherence ::: ## Self-check quiz (3/5) {.smaller} ::: {.quiz-q data-qid="z2q3" data-type="mcq" data-hash="693yww.y1n3ji" data-show="QSBiZXR0ZXIgZml0IGlzIG5vdCBhIGJldHRlciBjYXVzYWwgZXN0aW1hdGU7IGEgY29sbGlk ZXIgYWRkcyBiaWFz" data-explain="VmFyaWFibGVzIGFmZmVjdGVkIGJ5IHRoZSBleHBvc3VyZSBhbmQgdGhlIG91dGNvbWUgcHJl ZGljdCB0aGUgb3V0Y29tZSB3ZWxsLCB5ZXQgY29uZGl0aW9uaW5nIG9uIHRoZW0gYmlhc2Vz IHRoZSBlZmZlY3QuIENob29zZSBjb3ZhcmlhdGVzIGZyb20gdGhlIERBRy4="} The model that includes clinic visits has a higher R-squared but gives -8.8 mmHg. What is the lesson? - A better fit is not a better causal estimate; a collider adds bias - A model with a higher R-squared should be preferred for causal questions - The effect of the programme is truly -8.8 once clinic visits are held fixed - Clinic visits are a confounder that the first model failed to include ::: ## Self-check quiz (4/5) {.smaller} ::: {.quiz-q data-qid="z2q4" data-type="mcq" data-hash="694c5m.y1ni0w" data-show="SXQgcHJlZGljdHMgZWFjaCBvdXRjb21lIHVuZGVyIGJvdGggb3B0aW9ucyBhbmQgYXZlcmFn ZXMgdGhlIGRpZmZlcmVuY2U=" data-explain="UHJlZGljdGlvbnMgdW5kZXIgZXhwb3N1cmUgYW5kIHVuZGVyIG5vIGV4cG9zdXJlIGZvciB0 aGUgc2FtZSBwZW9wbGUgYXJlIGNvbXBhcmVkLCBhbmQgdGhlIGF2ZXJhZ2UgZGlmZmVyZW5j ZSBlc3RpbWF0ZXMgdGhlIGNhdXNhbCBlZmZlY3QgaW4gdGhhdCBwb3B1bGF0aW9uLg=="} What does standardisation (g-computation) do? - It divides each coefficient by its standard error to compare the effect sizes - It predicts each outcome under both options and averages the difference - It matches each enrolled adult with a non-enrolled adult of the same age - It rescales the covariates to a mean of zero and a variance of one ::: ## Self-check quiz (5/5) {.smaller} ::: {.quiz-q data-qid="z2q5" data-type="mcq" data-hash="694ped.y1nwib" data-show="VGhlIGVucm9sbGVkIGhhdmUgYSBoaWdoZXIgYmFzZWxpbmUgU0JQLCB3aGVyZSB0aGUgcHJv Z3JhbW1lIHdvcmtzIGJldHRlcg==" data-explain="VGhlIGVmZmVjdCBpbmNyZWFzZXMgd2l0aCBiYXNlbGluZSBTQlAsIGFuZCB0aGUgZW5yb2xs ZWQgaGF2ZSBoaWdoZXIgdmFsdWVzLiBBdmVyYWdpbmcgb3ZlciB0aGVtIGdpdmVzIGEgbGFy Z2VyIGVmZmVjdCB0aGFuIGF2ZXJhZ2luZyBvdmVyIGV2ZXJ5b25lLg=="} The ATT (-6.6) is larger than the ATE (-6.2). What explains this? - The ATT is computed with fewer adults, so it is biased away from zero by chance - The ATE includes adults whose data are missing at the twelve-month visit - The ATT is adjusted for adherence to medication, and the ATE is not - The enrolled have a higher baseline SBP, where the programme works better ::: ## Score and take-home **Your score: ** ::: {.incremental} - Adjust for **confounders** from the DAG: −6.3 vs naive −1.4 - **Mediator** → direct effect only; **collider** → bias - **R² is not a guide**; only the exposure row is causal - **g-computation**: predict under both options, average - Say whether you estimate the **ATE** or the **ATT** ::: **Next:** Session 3: propensity scores and matching

<script>
  // htmlwidgets need to know to resize themselves when slides are shown/hidden.
  // Fire the "slideenter" event (handled by htmlwidgets.js) when the current
  // slide changes (different for each slide format).
  (function () {
    // dispatch for htmlwidgets
    function fireSlideEnter() {
      const event = window.document.createEvent("Event");
      event.initEvent("slideenter", true, true);
      window.document.dispatchEvent(event);
    }

    function fireSlideChanged(previousSlide, currentSlide) {
      fireSlideEnter();

      // dispatch for shiny
      if (window.jQuery) {
        if (previousSlide) {
          window.jQuery(previousSlide).trigger("hidden");
        }
        if (currentSlide) {
          window.jQuery(currentSlide).trigger("shown");
        }
      }
    }

    // hookup for slidy
    if (window.w3c_slidy) {
      window.w3c_slidy.add_observer(function (slide_num) {
        // slide_num starts at position 1
        fireSlideChanged(null, w3c_slidy.slides[slide_num - 1]);
      });
    }

  })();
</script>
